title: Preserve member identity without widening local-operator authority
summary: Carry the current member through every transport and recovery boundary while keeping device-owner capabilities explicitly separate.
reusable_steps: Carry the current member through every transport and recovery boundary while keeping device-owner capabilities explicitly separate
expected_outcome: When a browser stores a member bearer separately from its cookie, verify all request paths, including indirect library fetches, event streams and downloads. A successful sign-in page does not prove later API calls use the same principal. Use an explicit same-origin allowlisted member transport, normalize Headers, reject redirects, and fence response and body completion against abort, token and authentication revision changes. Keep rejected or unavailable credentials fail-closed; never clear and retry as a credential-free loopback operator. Verify persistence before enabling first-run continuation, preserve an already-issued token for storage retry, and abort or invalidate repeated and interrupted sign-in attempts. Native EventSource and anchor downloads cannot carry a tab bearer: choose paced authenticated polling and bounded authenticated attachment streaming instead. Keep transport transformations compatible with exact byte validation, including no-transform when Content-Length is authoritative. Explicit logout must clear the tab bearer and scoped drafts only after the existing server logout validation, with honest blocked-storage recovery. Local-only operator service, OAuth, secrets and personal-avatar capabilities require their original authority boundary and must not be swept into a global interceptor. Validate with stale/ABA authentication, storage failures, repeat/cancel/unmount/Back navigation, stream limits and object-URL cleanup tests. Synthetic fixtures and builds do not establish live account issuance or provider connectivity.
